note: Planted problems and decoys for the audit. A reported finding matches a planted one when it names the same kind and file and a line within 1 of the evidence line (the loop line or the query line, for example). Decoys are correct code that looks like a problem; flagging one is a false alarm. Kinds are fixed: see `kinds`.

planted.abuse: If JWT_SECRET is unset in production, anyone who reads this repository can sign their own admin token.
planted.fix: Fail at startup when JWT_SECRET is missing; never fall back to a value written in code.

planted.abuse: The search text is pasted into SQL, so a crafted q can read or change any table.
planted.fix: Pass the value as a parameter: LIKE $1 with ['%' + q + '%'].

planted.abuse: Anyone, logged in or not, can delete any user; every other user route requires a login.
planted.fix: Add auth.required and auth.admin, as the role route does.

planted.abuse: Returns every order of every customer, unpaged: a data leak and a slow, memory-heavy response as the table grows.
planted.fix: Filter by req.user.id and add LIMIT with paging.

planted.has: SELECT sku, qty FROM order_items WHERE order_id = $1
planted.abuse: One query per order (up to 51 round trips per request); slow under load.
planted.fix: Fetch all items once with order_id = ANY($1), as /orders/summary does.

planted.abuse: Every server error sends the stack trace to the client, showing file paths, libraries and code structure.
planted.fix: Log the error on the server and send a generic message.

planted.abuse: Unlimited login attempts allow password guessing; no rate limiter exists anywhere in the app.
planted.fix: Limit attempts per IP and per account (for example express-rate-limit) on /login.

planted.abuse: Debug mode returns full tracebacks to clients on errors.
planted.fix: Leave debug off, or read it from a setting that is off in production.

planted.abuse: Any website may call the API from a visitor's browser, and credentials are allowed too.
planted.fix: List the real front-end origins; keep allow_credentials only for those.

planted.has: text(f"SELECT id, name FROM user WHERE name = '{name}'")
planted.abuse: The name is pasted into SQL with an f-string; a crafted name can read or change any table.
planted.fix: Use a bound parameter, as /users/by-name-safe does.

planted.abuse: One query per user (up to 101 per request).
planted.fix: Fetch notes for all user ids at once (Note.owner_id.in_(ids)) and group them.

planted.abuse: Users are looked up by email (main.py) but the column has no index, so each lookup scans the whole table.
planted.fix: Field(index=True, unique=True) on email, with a migration.

planted.abuse: Returns every note of every user, unpaged.
planted.fix: Filter to the caller's notes and add limit and offset.
